title: cuda-graph: add capture/replay with shape guards and prewarm to reduce warmup regressions
author: Marcus Lee
description:
Motivation: CUDA graph capture/replay can significantly reduce per-token overhead on GPU-backed inference, but earlier attempts introduced warmup regressions for workloads with variable shapes and dynamic batching. This PR implements a robust capture/replay flow with explicit shape guards and an optional prewarm path to avoid regression windows on first requests.

What this PR does: - Adds a graph cache keyed by shape-guard signatures and device/kernel configuration. - Introduces a shape guard table that conservatively matches incoming input shapes to cached graphs; guards are kept minimal to maximize reuse while ensuring correctness. - Implements an explicit prewarm flow that captures canonical graphs during model initialization for common batch/seq length combos. Prewarm is opt-in via config and enabled by default for dedicated deployments. - Adds fallback logic when graph replay fails (e.g., kernel mismatch) to fall back to the non-graph path and emit a metric; includes a bounded retry to avoid causing hot loops. - Adds instrumentation: graph_cache.hit/miss counters, guard_mismatch, prewarm_success/failure, and a sampling trace of capture duration. - Adds integration tests to exercise capture/replay across variable batch sizes and sequence lengths and a micro-benchmark to measure p50/p95 token latency.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of graph capture/replay core 
- [x] Shape guard matching and conservative fallback
- [x] Prewarm path with config toggle
- [x] Metrics and tracing hooks
- [x] Integration tests and perf micro-bench
- [x] Docs: brief guidance added to docs/perf/cuda-graphs.md

Notes on regressions: During early dogfood we observed a regression where uncommon shapes caused repeated misses and extra memory churn during capture, increasing p95 for bursty traffic. The changes in this PR reduce capture churn by: 1) expanding guard matching to group similar shapes into a single canonical guard, 2) prewarming the most common graphs on cold start, and 3) emitting a metric and fast fallback to prevent repeated failed captures.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: The prewarm behavior is opt-in (config true for internal dedicated infra); capture/replay falls back cleanly, so there is no correctness break for existing deployments.

Testing and verification: Unit tests for graph cache/guard logic, integration test using the GPU CI runner to validate correctness across batches [1..8] and seq lengths {64,128,256,512}. Perf micro-bench demonstrates improvements (see perf_results).

Related: ENG-1342 (graph replay platform work), ENG-1379 (kv cache and scheduling follow-ups).

review_conversation: Ava Patel: Great direction. Two concerns: (1) shape guards might be too granular and reduce reuse; can we add a heuristic to collapse near shapes? (requested changes)
Marcus Lee: Addressed by adding a size-bucketing heuristic and a unit test (see shape_guard.cpp:bucket_for_shape). Updated the test to cover bucketing behavior.
Sofia Ramirez: Need a safe fallback if capture fails more than once in a short window to avoid repeated allocation churn. (requested changes)
Marcus Lee: Added a 'capture_backoff' metric and fast-fail path after 3 consecutive failures per model-device pair. Also emits guard_mismatch metric so ops can be monitored.
Jian Chen: Can we gate prewarm behind a config with default disabled for public hosted tier? Also add documentation for memory impact. (comment)
Marcus Lee: Prewarm is opt-in; we set default true for dedicated infra and false for hosted. Docs updated with memory and perf tradeoffs.
release_notes: Add CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards and optional prewarm. Improves p50/p95 token latency and reduces warmup regressions for dedicated deployments. Prewarm is configurable and off by default for hosted tier.
perf_results: Micro-bench (seq512, batch=1..8): p50 token latency reduced ~12%, p95 reduced ~18% on A100; throughput +10% for steady-state workloads.
Cold-start warmup window reduced: first-request overhead from ~120ms -> ~45ms for prewarmed graphs on common shapes.
Workloads with highly variable shapes still see a small capture penalty on rare shapes but are bounded by fast fallback and backoff.
notes: Follow-ups: (1) integrate with KV cache to allow mixed prefix reuse (ENG-1405), (2) add async capture path to reduce blocking on first capture, (3) expose guard_mismatch alert in console.
